alert.title: Checkout errors spiking after Friday deploy
alert.symptoms: Checkout requests failing with database connection errors; p99 latency 4.9s, error rate 25%, starting about 10 minutes after the v2.6.0 Friday deploy.

response.root_cause: Connection pool exhaustion in payments-api after v2.6.0 deploy, causing PostgreSQL to reject new connections (remaining connection slots reserved for superuser)
response.blast_radius: All checkout transactions through payments-api are failing, affecting any customer attempting to purchase, leading to revenue loss and potential churn
first_actions: Inspect DB connection pool usage and pg_stat_activity for runaway connections
Rollback or hot-fix the v2.6.0 release of payments-api
Temporarily increase PostgreSQL max_connections or restart the payments-api service to clear connections

response.root_cause: The checkout failures are caused by the recurring order‑confirmation retry path that opens a new PostgreSQL session for each retry and never releases it on timeout, exhausting the 20‑connection pool (as seen in INC-002).
response.blast_radius: All checkout requests on payments‑api experience elevated latency (p99 ~5s) and a ~25% error rate, affecting any user attempting to complete a purchase during peak Friday traffic.

New alert: Checkout errors spiking after Friday deploy. Service: payments-api, severity: SEV1.
Symptoms: Checkout requests failing with database connection errors; p99 latency 4.9s, error rate 25%, starting about 10 minutes after the v2.6.0 Friday deploy.
Error: org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections

Evidence (only these incidents may be cited):
Incident INC-002 (payments-api, SEV1, 2026-05-15T14:32:10Z):
Symptoms: payments-api p99 latency above 4.8s and checkout error rate above 23% starting ~12 minutes after the v2.3.0 Friday deploy; new checkouts failing with DB connection errors.
Root cause: The v2.3.0 deploy's new order-confirmation retry path opens a DB session per retry without releasing it on timeout, exhausting the 20-connection Postgres pool within minutes of Friday peak traffic.
Resolver: Priya Nair

Incident INC-021 (payments-api, SEV1, 2026-08-28T15:55:08Z):
Symptoms: Same signature as INC-002/INC-009/INC-017: p99 latency above 4.9s and checkout errors above 24% about 8 minutes after the v2.5.0 Friday deploy.
Root cause: Fourth occurrence of the same unfixed order-confirmation session leak, triggered by the v2.5.0 Friday deploy.
Resolver: Priya Nair

Incident INC-009 (payments-api, SEV1, 2026-06-19T15:10:47Z):
Symptoms: Same signature as INC-002: p99 latency above 4.6s and checkout errors above 20% about 15 minutes after the v2.3.1 Friday deploy.
Root cause: Same order-confirmation retry session leak as INC-002 (still unfixed in code), triggered again by Friday deploy traffic.
Resolver: Priya Nair

Incident INC-017 (payments-api, SEV1, 2026-07-24T14:48:51Z):
Symptoms: Same signature as INC-002/INC-009: p99 latency above 4.7s and checkout errors above 22% about 10 minutes after the v2.4.0 Friday deploy.
Root cause: Same unresolved order-confirmation session leak, now triggered a third time by the v2.4.0 Friday deploy.
Resolver: Priya Nair

Ranked fixes (use the top one as first_actions[0]):
  1. increase_postgres_pool_size (score=+0.660, worked=3, partial=0, failed=0, recent_failures=0)
